connection_condition: cards.setCode corresponds to sets.code; every distinct setCode in cards resolves to exactly one set
description: A card set is composed of the printings released within it, and a printing has no meaning outside the product it was printed in.

connection_condition: set_translations.setCode corresponds to sets.code; no translation row references an unknown set
description: A set's localized names are part of the set record and cannot exist without the set.

connection_condition: foreign_data.uuid corresponds to cards.uuid; at most one translation row per card and language
description: A printing's localized versions are part of that printing; a translation row is meaningless without the card it localizes.

connection_condition: legalities.uuid corresponds to cards.uuid; one legality row per card and format
description: A printing carries one legality record per format it has been evaluated for; the record depends on the card it describes.

connection_condition: rulings.uuid corresponds to cards.uuid; every ruling resolves to a card
description: Official rulings are attached to the card they clarify and have no independent existence.

connection_condition: printings share the card name text column rather than a separate card identity identifier
description: A named card is realised by one or more printings; each printing exists as an instance of that named card.

connection_condition: foreign_data.language and set_translations.language are different columns that draw on the same language vocabulary; all ten languages present in set_translations also occur in foreign_data
description: Language of a card translation and language of a set-name translation denote the same business concept recorded in two different tables.
Ruling count is derived by counting ruling entries per card; the card with the most ruling information is the maximum of this derived count.
A percentage over cards is derived by dividing the count of printings satisfying a condition by a chosen printing population.
A promotional printing is a kind of printing; promotional printings form a subset of the printing population.
A borderless printing is a kind of printing, distinguished by its border colour value.
A foreign-only set is a kind of set; the flagged sets form a small subset of all sets.
Card subtypes refine the broader card type classification, but the two are stored as separate text columns with different value domains and different coverage.
A legality record states a card's status within one format, so the status is only meaningful relative to that format.
Each card translation is written in exactly one language, which categorises the translation record.
Each set-name translation is written in exactly one language, which categorises the translation record.
The textless flag and the stored rules text describe the same text box but disagree on 1070 printings, so they are related yet not interchangeable.
A printing's foil availability is recorded through external purchase identifiers attached to the printing row.
